sections.content: How many people are "financial and accounting technicians"?

14,685 people

were counted on the census as "financial and accounting technicians" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Financial and accounting technicians work alongside accountants and other financial professionals in managing the financial affairs of organisations.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "financial and accounting technicians" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "financial and accounting technicians", 16.3% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "financial and accounting technicians" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "financial and accounting technicians" included:

  • production and process engineers
  • teachers of english as a foreign language
  • therapy professionals (other)

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "financial and accounting technicians" there were more women than men (59% compared with 41%).

This means "financial and accounting technicians" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "business and public service associate professionals".

Men made up 41% and women made up 59% of "financial and accounting technicians"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "financial and accounting technicians" included:

  • business associate professionals (other)
  • optometrists
  • marketing and commercial managers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "financial and accounting technicians" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged under 30 years old, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "financial and accounting technicians" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "financial and accounting technicians", 7.9% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (80.6% compared with 19.4%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (96.2%) than self-employed (3.8%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
